newsitem.title: USA: CBOE details planned options on Dow Jones averages.
newsitem.headline: CBOE details planned options on Dow Jones averages.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange set contract specifications for options on the three main Dow Jones averages, the exchange said Wednesday.
Pending U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approval, the exchange expects to launch the options later this year.

"With options based on 1/100th of the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI and a standard industry multiplier of 100, each options contract will represent the market value of the DJIA," CBOE chairman and chief executive officer William Brodsky said in a statement.

"For example, if the Dow is at 7,820, options on the DJIA will be based on an index level of 78.20," he said. "Given the standard multiplier of $100, the underlying value for the options would be $7,820."

Options on the Dow transportation average .DJT will be based on one-tenth of the average's level, and options on the Dow utility average .DJU will be based on the full value of the average. Both will have multipliers of 100.
Position limits will be one million contracts for options on the industrials and 15,000 each for the other two averages.
The options will be settled in cash and will have European-style exercise, meaning they can be exercised only on the last day of trading before expiration.
The CBOE said strike prices for options on the Dow Jones industrials will be set to bracket the index level in increments of one-half or one point.
Strikes for transportation and utility average options will be set to bracket the indexes at increments of 2-1/2 or five points.
Earlier this month, Dow Jones & Co granted the CBOE a license to list options on the averages.
It also gave the Chicago Board of Trade a license to trade futures and futures-options and licensed the American Stock Exchange to trade a unit trust based on the average.
